title: Square One Bias in NLP: Towards a Multi-Dimensional Exploration of the Research Manifold

bias_targets.methodology: Manual classification and meta-analysis of 461 ACL 2021 oral papers to quantify the community's tendency to default to prototypical experimental setups, focusing on single-dimensional contributions rather than intersections of fairness, efficiency, multilinguality, and interpretability.

Annotating recent NLP research papers and textbooks to calculate the percentage that evaluate exclusively on English datasets, and conducting a literature review on how English-centric protocols disadvantage morphologically rich or free-word-order languages.
Qualitative analysis of how standard models and tokenizers (e.g., subword tokenization, sliding window attention) implicitly favor languages with limited morphology and strict word order.

Quantifying the percentage of ACL 2021 papers that optimize exclusively for standard performance metrics like accuracy or F1, ignoring multidimensional tradeoffs like computational efficiency or fairness.
